findings.passage: When you arrive at your polling place to vote, state law requires you to either show a picture ID or sign an affidavit attesting that you are not in possession of a picture ID.
findings.note: Voter's Guide published on her state Senate site. It describes the existing Michigan photo-ID rule and the affidavit option; it describes current law and does not say whether she wants it changed.

findings.passage: Note: If you do not bring a picture ID to the polls or do not own a picture ID, you can vote like any other voter by signing an affidavit that will be provided to you.
findings.note: Same Voter's Guide. Explains that a voter without photo ID signs an affidavit and votes like any other voter. Describes current law.
subjects: sworn statement for voters with no ID
